facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s presented with a persistent eruption of 5 years' duration
He had been treated with oral methotrexate for presumed chronic dermatitis
after treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy had failed
Investigation of medical records revealed a history of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks prior to the development of the current eruption at the same site
Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules clustered on the superior buttocks and intergluteal cleft bilaterally
The lesions were smooth and firm
Syphilis screen results were negative
Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band in a polyclonal background
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
Dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the upper dermis admixed with eosinophils and plasma cells
Epidermotropism was not identified
Second biopsy: Similar to prior findings, but with more dense and atypical infiltrate showing epidermotropism
